text:
maya: Gingerbay (tenant=gingerbay-prod-17) reporting p99 spikes on embeddings API since ~08:30 UTC. They said p95 looks fine but p99 jumps to ~3s-8s. Customer started seeing this after yesterday's model rollout. Attaching sample req ids and a short log snippet.

raj: Can you paste a couple of request IDs + tenant id? I want to check per-tenant queueing and node-level metrics.

maya: tenant: gingerbay-prod-17
reqs: req_02f3a7c9, req_02f3a8b1, req_02f3aef4
sample curl (redacted):
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \\  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","input":"<payload>"}'
```

logs (excerpt):
```
[08:31:02] req=req_02f3a7c9 tenant=gingerbay-prod-17 node=gpu-12 latency=812ms queue_ms=2100 memcpy_ms=340
[08:31:07] req=req_02f3a8b1 tenant=gingerbay-prod-17 node=gpu-12 latency=602ms queue_ms=1200 memcp_ms=310
[08:35:10] req=req_02f3aef4 tenant=gingerbay-prod-17 node=gpu-9  latency=110ms queue_ms=60 memcp_ms=30
```

sophie: Customer adds that the workload is bursty (bulk batch embedding jobs every 10-12 minutes). They said their traffic pattern increased after a marketing send.

raj: Looking at node metrics — gpu-12 shows high memcpy and long tail queueing starting ~08:25. There's another tenant running a large offload job on the same shard (noisy neighbor). Also see per-tenant gating kicking in which pushes their requests to lower-priority queue when burst depth grows.

raj: Proposed immediate mitigations:
- create a 1h reservation on a separate slice for gingerbay-prod-17 (min 1, burst 2)
- add gingerbay to temporary priority-lane allowlist for 1h (bypass per-tenant throttles)
- optionally set per-tenant soft throttle to 3 rps to smooth the burst if reservation not enough

maya: Can eng ops create the reservation and allowlist now? Customer is online. They asked for ETA ~15-20m.

raj: I'll run the admin flow now. Commands I'm using:
```bash
# create short-lived reservation
redwoodctl reservation create \\ 
  --tenant gingerbay-prod-17 \\ 
  --gpu-type a100 \\ 
  --min-instances 1 \\ 
  --burst-instances 2 \\ 
  --duration 1h \\ 
  --reason "emergency noisy-neighbor mitigation for gingerbay"

# add to priority allowlist
redwoodctl allowlist add \\ 
  --tenant gingerbay-prod-17 \\ 
  --policy priority-lane \\ 
  --expires-in 1h
```

infra-bot: Reservation res_9b12 created by raj at 2912341000. Node assignment: gpu-12 slice=3. Allowlist entry ALW-981 created, expires=2912344600.

maya: Pushed instructions to customer. They just reported an initial improvement: "we see p99 down to ~500ms for a few requests" (ack 2912341200).

raj: Verified metrics after reservation:
```
before (08:30): p95=210ms p99=3800ms queue_depth=18
after (08:36): p95=180ms p99=520ms queue_depth=3
```

sophie: Great. Follow-ups: schedule a postmortem with capacity team and customer success. Long-term recommendations to file:
- add per-tenant capacity smoothing (adaptive tokens)
- auto-detect noisy neighbor patterns and auto-evict or throttle heavy background jobs
- add fallback to smaller embedding model during high contention
- avoid major model rollouts during peak marketing windows (coordination with CS)

raj: I'll open INF-5423 to track the infra work (smoothing + detection + eviction policies). Also will add a change to the rollout checklist to flag high-risk customers during deploys.

maya: I'll keep the reservation + allowlist active for 1h and monitor. If stable for 24h we'll close. I'll update Gingerbay and share the postmortem invite. :white_check_mark:

sophie: Thanks team. I'll also ask Gingerbay for their bulk job schedule so we can propose rate-limiting or staggered backfills.

maya: closing notes: customer happy with immediate improvement, asked for a follow-up on long-term fixes. Will collect SLO graphs and paste into the ticket later.
